summary: The core observation is sharp: agents default to ease-in on enter animations, solid borders instead of shadows, and animate everything in sight, and Emil encodes each correction as a small installable skill file that any agent session can consume on demand. That maps directly onto how I think about PenguPool and AgentOn Pocket — the interesting layer isn't the model, it's the structured, composable knowledge you route into a session so it stops producing plausible-but-wrong output, and the "break-ui" skill (hit your UI with one-letter names, huge counts, empty lists before you ship) is the kind of cheap robustness check I wish more of my own agent workflows ran by default. The mobile-native and gesture skills are especially relevant to Oh Tidepool, where a 100vh bug or a stray tap-highlight flash is the whole gap between something that feels like an app and a website stretched onto a phone.
